medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The School of Medicine is committed to diversity in the faculty and the student body. Its goal is to recruit, admit and graduate students that comply with all the requirements. The office of Diversity Affairs has programs to assist to help meeting the objectives of all student body.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence:
Students may be granted leave of absence for justifiable reasons, including: 
(a) service in the United States Armed Forces; 
(b) education or research at another institution, or 
(c) personal or medical reasons. 

All leaves of absence will be for a maximum of one year, except for students with federal financial aid, who will not be allowed to take a leave of absence for a period exceeding six months. Any student requesting a leave of absence must submit a written request stating the reasons that justify the leave. The Associate Dean of Student Affairs, after an interview, will evaluate the request and submit a written report to the President/Dean. In order to consider a leave of absence, certain requirements must be met. The student 
(a) shall complete all courses of the previous academic semester,

medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Student Organizations  The Office of the Associate Dean of Student Affairs encourages student organizations. Any group of students interested in organizing an association with religious, sports, cultural, and academic purposes is welcome to do so. The School requires that their activities relate to the school's objectives. Those interested should inform the Associate Dean of Student Affairs of their intention in order for their organization to be officially recognized.  

General Students Council (GSC) -  The GSC is organized to insure full participation for students in all matters regarding their studies and relationship with the San Juan Bautista Medical School. It constitutes the official forum where analysis, discussions and study of the student's needs and aspirations are done, and where opinions are put forth, regarding any problems or issues related to the community as a whole. Students who are interested in becoming a member must meet the requirements listed in the Student Rule
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The School's facilities are located on the grounds of the Menonita Hospital Center (formerly San Juan Bautista Medical Center). The 52 acre campus is the location for the Hospital and the School, which houses administrative offices, the biomedical sciences faculty, and the Library/Learning Resources Center, as well as the classrooms and laboratories for teaching and research. Clinical training at the Menonita Hospital Center brings students into contact with a patient population drawn from many different socio-economic groups. The Menonita Hospital Center is the principal clinical training facility for third and fourth year students.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: The School provides information about available housing facilities in Caguas.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The SJBSM through the Equal Access, Diversity and Inclusion Policy is actively involved in the support of gender and sexual minority students on campus. Gender and sexual minority students are also well represented through our LGBTQ Student Interest Group
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The school has an intensive program to reinforce the academic quality of students. The program begins with the admission process and continues in successive stages during the academic program to detect and manage academic risks and difficulties. Program actions and activities include workshops, assessment sessions, and group and individual tutorials, among others. All students receive pertinent information about this program during orientation week.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: San Juan Bautista School of Medicine (SJB) offers an inclusive campus culture that promotes community, collaboration, and support among students, faculty, and staff. Located in Caguas, Puerto Rico, SJB blends urban and natural surroundings, emphasizing both academic rigor and a commitment to community service. Its diverse student body participates in various extracurricular activities, from medical organizations to outreach programs addressing health needs in underserved areas. SJB fosters involvement in cultural events, seminars, and workshops, broadening students’ perspectives on health issues unique to Puerto Rican and Latin American populations. Campus life is enriched by proximity to the San Juan metro area, scenic landscapes, and cultural sites, offering students a balanced lifestyle with ample recreational and social opportunities. This mix of rigorous academics and community engagement shapes SJB students for compassionate, culturally attuned medical practice.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Tutoring are offered for students performing under 70% on the course grades.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Clinical skills sessions involving volunteer patients start during the first year. Real patient interaction begins at the third year.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Traditional in-person and online lectures, Self-Directed Learning (e-Forums, On-line Self-study Lectures & virtual modules), Interactive case discussions, clinical skills sessions
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: The clinical phase of medical school begins in the third year at affiliated teaching hospitals throughout the Island and United States.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: SJBSM had defined its curriculum within a student-centered approach, highlighting the values, attitudes, and social responsibility of the practice of medicine. It facilitates active learning and integration, offering early exposure to clinical scenarios and technological experiences in the learning process and using diverse assessment methodologies. The curriculum is structured in five emphases: medical knowledge, clinical skills, research and information literacy, professionalism and community awareness. These emphases are incorporated throughout the four years. The preclinical courses are offered in a system-based approach during the first two years. The third year is devoted to core clinical clerkships, both inpatient and outpatient scenarios, including a research clerkship. The fourth year reinforces the practice of medicine with core and electives sub-internships.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: 1. Offer and maintain an interdisciplinary, updated primary care medical education program of a moral, humanistic, community-based and ethical nature with high academic and scientific standards.     2. Focus the medical education curriculum on professionalism and humanistic community-bases medicine, within a continuous and coordinated framework for patient care.     3. Create an academic community-based medical education environment that is conducive to academic freedom and commitment to excellence where medical students, faculty, and support personnel are motivated to learn, teach, and collaborate.     4. Provide medical students with research experience related to community-based and primary care medicine, and basis sciences.     5. Operate as an academic health services center that promotes active community participation.     6. Provide and adequate distribution of resources and a solid financial basis to support the medical education program.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The School of Medicine was founded in 1978 in San Juan, Puerto Rico, as a not-for-profit corporation, incorporated under the laws of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. It is located in Caguas, Puerto Rico, one of the most important urban centers. It is authorized by the Puerto Rico Council on Higher Education to offer studies leading to the M.D. degree. The MSCHE granted accreditation to the School in 2004. The LCME reaccredited the academic program on 2019. As of June 30, 2010, the School of Medicine has graduated a total of 1035 medical doctors who have been successfully integrated in their communities as competent and caring health providers, both in Puerto Rico and abroad.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: We are committed to educating a diverse generation of physicians and other health professionals.  Graduates will have the knowledge, skills, values and competence to pursue career options in medicine, deliver high quality care, and conduct clinical research.  The school’s special interest is centered on community health, conducting research on translational community medicine, and on graduating physicians who are responsive to the health needs of underserved and medically vulnerable populations.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: SJBSM exhibits a thorough approach to medical student selection, assignment, and progression through a comprehensive and holistic admissions process. Each applicant is assessed on academic qualifications, life experiences, and core personal attributes, ensuring a well-rounded evaluation. Key selection criteria include a Bachelor (BS,BA) Degree, GPA, MCAT scores, personal essays, extracurricular / clinical experience and multiple -mini-interviews, providing a balanced assessment of candidates' academic readiness, interpersonal skills, and resilience

medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The San Juan Bautista School of Medicine’s Technical Standards define the essential physical, cognitive, emotional, and interpersonal abilities required for admission, progression, and graduation, ensuring patient and student safety. Consistent with AAMC guidance and the ADA, students must complete the curriculum independently, with or without reasonable accommodations. Competence is required in five areas: Observation (accurate sensory assessment of patients and scientific material), Communication (clear oral, written, digital, and bilingual English/Spanish interaction), Motor (performance of physical exams and clinical and emergency procedures), Intellectual (reasoning, problem-solving, data integration, and clinical judgment), and Behavioral/Social Attributes (professionalism, teamwork, resilience, integrity, and compassion). Students must attest to compliance annually, and those unable to meet standards, with or without accommodation, may not continue in the program.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The Financial Aid Office counsels students regarding the availability of economic aid and the procedure to file up applications. For further information, please refer to: https://www.sanjuanbautista.edu/admissions/financial-aid
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Within ten (10) calendar days following the notification of admission, the student must pay a $100 deposit in order to reserve his/her seat. This amount is refundable until May 15, and it will be credited toward tuition and fees.  The Bursar's Office is responsible for collecting the tuition and fees student incur at the time of registration, in addition to other fees such as credit transcripts and certificates, among others. The Bursar's Office is in charge of processing checks received from Stafford Loans and of generating the checks from the Supplementary Aid Program and other financial aid received by students.  Payment Plans: The School offers an alternative payment plan to students, who for some reason do not qualify to receive a Stafford Loan, and cannot pay the total tuition fee during registration. medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Coursework must consist of at least ninety (90) credits, including the following required courses: General chemistry (8), organic chemistry (8), General physics (8). General biology (8), Behavioral and social sciences (9), Spanish (9), English (9) and electives (28; with Anatomy, Cellular / Molecular Biology, Biochemistry as recommended courses).
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Admissions office evaluates all applications, taking into consideration academic and personal qualifications in an holistic way. The analysis includes academic achievement, premedical studies required for admission to the program, and MCAT scores. If it is found competitive, the candidate is invited for an interview. The motivations to study medicine, leadership qualities, ability to relate to other people and deal with problems, past experience in community/scientific activities and how culturally and linguistically diverse is the candidate are also taken into consideration by the Admission's Committee.
